## STEP 0 — GROUND: ASSERT FAILED. Run halted.

**0.1 `roll_call`** returned exactly **one** knowledge base, and pagination confirms it is the complete list (`totalItems: 1, totalPages: 1, hasNextPage: false`):

| knowledgeId | repoSlug | type | lastIndexedCommit | commits indexed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `caa863cc-241f-5eec-83d7-5e53d9029e12` | `calcom/cal.diy` (formerly `calcom/cal.com`) | CODE | `176037d0afbe572f870a3c702985e7cd83fe6c0c` | 20 |

**0.3 `rap_sheet`** (no arguments) corroborates this: 20 rows, all 20 belonging to that same single repository — "an open-source scheduling infrastructure and appointment booking platform." There is no second repository behind the paging.

### Absent repositories — all 16 of the ROSTER

`redux`, `redux-toolkit`, `react-redux`, `reselect`, `react`, `jotai`, `zustand`, `db`, `xyflow`, `query`, `table`, `tldraw`, `redux-devtools`, `router`, `primitives`, `zod`.

Not one of them appears in `roll_call` as a `repoSlug`, and none appears in `formerSlugs` (the only rename recorded anywhere is `calcom/cal.com` → `calcom/cal.diy`, which is not a roster repo). The ROSTER pins are therefore not "an older snapshot that is also indexed" — the 0.1 escape clause about pin-vs-tip drift does not apply here, because the *repositories themselves* are missing, not merely a commit of them.

### Why I am not proceeding

STEP 0.1's failure branch is explicit: **STOP and say so plainly; answering from memory about a repository that is not indexed is never acceptable.** Every remaining step is downstream of a `knowledgeId` I cannot obtain:

- STEP 2 requires `|ob.repos| >= 4` drawn from indexed repositories — there is one, and it is not on the roster.
- STEP 3.2 requires `knowledgeId = <that repo>` **set** for every stakeout; the only legal value points at a scheduling platform that holds none of the roster's code.
- STEP 6.7 requires every emitted path to have been **returned by a call**. With the roster unindexed, any path I could name — and I can picture several plausible ones in `tldraw`, `query`, `xyflow` and elsewhere — would be reconstructed from memory, which 6.7 voids and 0.1 forbids outright.

Producing a ranked list under these conditions would be fabrication wearing a citation, which is precisely the failure mode this algorithm's STEP 0 exists to prevent. I did not run any search, so nothing entered SWEPT, SEEN, CONFIRMED or CANDIDATES; there is no partial answer to salvage and no OPEN-obligation ledger to print, because OB[] was never allowed to reach STEP 3.

### What would unblock this

The 16 roster repositories need to be indexed into this session's org (`36af0f7a-fdf4-4497-9795-19d263268800`), each at least at the pinned commit given in the ROSTER. Once `roll_call` lists them, I can run the algorithm from STEP 0 in a fresh session — note that R1 forbids resuming this case, so it would need to be a new run rather than a continuation of this one.

One thing worth checking on your side: the case directory name and the roster suggest this session was expected to be pointed at a different plumbline org or index than the one it actually connected to. The org it reached holds only `calcom/cal.diy`, which looks like a configuration mismatch rather than a missing-index problem.
